:::{#exm-classification}
#### A diagnostic test as a classification rule

In a [binary classification problem](#def-binary-classification),
a COVID-19 test assigns each person tested to one of $K = 2$ [classes](#def-class),
$k_1 =$ "has COVID-19" or $k_0 =$ "does not have COVID-19",
based on a single feature $x$:
whether the test's result is "positive" or "negative".
The test is the [classification rule](#def-classification-rule)
that assigns a positive result to $k_1$
and a negative result to $k_0$:

$$
c(x) \eqdef
\begin{cases}
\text{has COVID-19} & \text{if } x = \text{positive} \\
\text{does not have COVID-19} & \text{if } x = \text{negative}
\end{cases}
$$ {#eq-classification-exm}

For a person drawn from a [population](exploratory-descriptive.qmd#def-population) with test result $X$,
the event that the test is [positive](#def-positive-classification) is $\posclass = \set{c(X) = \text{has COVID-19}}$,
and the event that the test is [negative](#def-negative-classification) is $\negclass = \set{c(X) = \text{does not have COVID-19}}$.
:::
